newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-DEVILS GOALTENDER BRODEUR SCORES PLAYOFF GOAL.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-DEVILS GOALTENDER BRODEUR SCORES PLAYOFF GOAL.

text.p: New Jersey Devils goaltender Martin Brodeur became just the second National Hockey League netminder to score a goal in a playoff game when he fired the puck into an empty Montreal Canadiens net on Thursday night.

Brodeur, who also made 28 saves, capped the Devils' scoring with his empty-netter with 45 seconds left in New Jersey's 5-2 win in the opening game of their first-round Eastern Conference playoff series with Montreal.
"It's unbelievable, it's a great feeling," said Brodeur, whose huge grin and obvious delight after the puck went in was visible even behind his mask.
Brodeur retrieved a loose puck from behind his goal, skated around the net and flipped the puck high into the air. It bounced at mid-ice and skittered into the Montreal net.
"I put a lot on it. I was trying to score," admitted Brodeur. "Dougie Gilmour got the puck for me," he said of his prized souvenir.
Philadelphia's Ron Hextall was the first goalie to score in the playoffs on April 11, 1989, against Washington.
Hextall was also the first NHL goalie to score by shooting the puck into the net in a regular season game when he scored against Boston in 1987.
